title: Operate and recover a local JAX workload
hardware: CPU; optional target runtime requires separate validation

stages.title: Real process lifecycle
stages.evidence: Success, runtime rejection and reaped timeout traces
stages.diagnosis: Check observed backend, last event, stderr and the actual child exit before retrying.

stages.title: Workload observability
stages.evidence: Raw structured events and independently recomputed throughput boundaries
stages.diagnosis: Count examples once and synchronize completed updates before timing.

stages.title: Complete-state recovery
stages.diagnosis: Inspect momentum, key, step and provenance rather than only final loss.

stages.title: Artifact selection and rollback
stages.evidence: Content IDs, failed gate and unchanged pointer, tested rollback
stages.diagnosis: Verify stored payload digests and prior compatibility before changing the pointer.

stages.title: Capacity and cost
stages.evidence: Measured local service time plus separately labeled demand, reserve and price assumptions
stages.diagnosis: Carry seconds-to-hours conversion, idle reservation and failure overhead explicitly.

rubric: Observe actual worker exit and reap timed-out processes
Derive useful metrics from synchronized work with explicit units
Rehearse failure and verify complete-state next-update recovery
Reject corrupted or incompatible checkpoint provenance
Publish, gate, atomically select and roll back exact content IDs
Separate measured workload duration from hypothetical demand and prices
Keep a runbook grounded in the actual failure trace and target limitations
setupNote: Work from the extracted top folder containing requirements-cpu.txt and projects/workload-operations. The checks use bounded local subprocesses and temporary directories; no cloud allocation occurs.
